t.3.73.1: Bṛhadaśva said: But Damayantī, having heard that, became deeply overwhelmed with grief, and suspecting that he was indeed Nala, she spoke these words to Keśinī.
t.3.73.2: Go again, Keśinī, and put Bāhuka to the test; staying near him without speaking, observe his conduct.
t.3.73.3: And whenever he does anything, O lovely lady, and whatever his reason for it, his conduct as he goes about it is to be closely observed by you.
t.3.73.4: And, O beautiful lady, to hinder him, not even fire should be given to him; if he asks, water is not to be given either, while you carefully take your time.
t.3.73.5: Having observed all this conduct carefully, report it to me; and whatever else you may see, that too must be told to me by you.
t.3.73.6: Thus addressed by Damayantī, Keśinī then went quickly, and having observed the signs of the one skilled with horses, she came back again.
t.3.73.7: She reported to Damayantī all of that just as it had happened, the sign, both divine and human, that had then been seen in Bāhuka.
t.3.73.8: Surely he is a man of pure conduct; never before, Damayantī, have I anywhere seen or even heard of a human being of that kind.
t.3.73.10: And for the sake of Ṛtuparṇa, food of many kinds was sent there by the king, and a great quantity of the meat of animals.
t.3.73.9: Coming upon a low passage, he never stoops anywhere; rather, on seeing him, the passage rises up as the obstruction requires, so that he goes at ease. Even in a narrow strait a very large and ample opening appears for him.
t.3.73.11: A pitcher had been set there for washing him; that pitcher, merely looked at by him, then became full.
t.3.73.13: Then the fire, the bearer of oblations, suddenly blazed up there; having seen that most wondrous thing, I have come here in amazement.
t.3.73.12: Then, having done the washing, Bāhuka set the vessel on the hearth, and taking up a handful of grass and whirling it about, he laid it in place to kindle it.
t.3.73.14: And I observed another very great wonder in him, O lovely one: even when he touches fire, he is not burned at all.
t.3.73.15: At his mere wish the water, once poured out, flows swiftly. And I have seen another wonder, exceedingly great indeed.
t.3.73.16: When he picked up flowers and slowly crushed them with his hands, then those flowers, even as they were being crushed by his palms,
t.3.73.18: Bṛhadaśva said: But Damayantī, having heard of that conduct of the one of holy renown, believed that Nala had arrived, revealed by his deeds and behavior.
t.3.73.17: And they become even more fragrant and fresh. Having seen these things, which are almost miracles, I have come here quickly.
t.3.73.19: Suspecting that Bāhuka was in truth her husband Nala in another form, she, weeping, spoke again to Keśinī in a gentle voice.
t.3.73.20: Go again, O beautiful woman, and while Bāhuka is not paying attention, take from the kitchen the cooked meat he has prepared and come back.
t.3.73.21: Going there while Bāhuka was busy, she took away some of that meat, still very hot, and then, swift and eager to please, Keśinī at that very moment gave it to Damayantī, O joy of the Kurus.
t.3.73.22: She, who in former days had often been accustomed to meat cooked by Nala, tasted it, and, deeming the cook to be Nala, she cried out, deeply grieved.
t.3.73.23: Having fallen into the utmost distress, and then having washed his face, he sent the pair of children back with Keśinī, O Bhārata.
t.3.73.24: Recognizing Indrasenā together with her brother, Bāhuka the king then ran to them, embraced them, and took them onto his lap.
t.3.73.25: But Bāhuka, approaching his two sons, who were like the sons of the gods, wept aloud, his heart utterly overwhelmed with grief.
t.3.73.26: But the Naiṣadha, having then repeatedly shown his agitation, suddenly let go of his two sons and said this to Keśinī:
t.3.73.27: Good lady, this pair closely resembles my own two children; that is why, the moment I saw them, I suddenly shed tears.
t.3.73.28: If you keep coming here so often, people may suspect you of some wrongdoing, and we are only guests from a foreign land. Go, good lady; homage to you.
